title: Etaleness near a regular coordinate fibre
statement: Let p:X→S be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and i:Y→X a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let a,b≥0, h:X→A^(a+b)_S over S, and v:Y→A^a_S etale [def-sbc-affine-space, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Assume the square formed by v,i,h and the inclusion setting the last b coordinates to zero is cartesian [def-pc-base-change]. Assume on every affine open of X the pullbacks of those b coordinates are weakly regular [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Then for each y∈Y there is an open neighbourhood T of i(y) such that h restricted to T is etale. This is a criterion for a specified map h; no coordinates are constructed.

source.place: Tag 0FUE, lemma-etale-local-structure, last two proof paragraphs: finite presentation, fibre dimension comparison, miracle flatness, fibre criterion and etale criterion

proof.text: Work on affine base and source neighbourhoods of the images of y. Write the base as Spec R and X as Spec A, and put f_j=h*(t_(a+j)). Finite-presentation permanence makes h finitely presented since p is smooth and affine-space projection is finitely presented. The cartesian hypothesis identifies Y with A/(f); etaleness of v makes this quotient smooth, flat and finitely presented over R. The weak regularity hypothesis becomes regularity after localizing at y, since the quotient has that point. Put k=κ(s) for the base point s. Apply [lem-pur-relative-regular-equations-base-change] to these flat algebras; the f_j form a regular sequence in L=O_(X_s),y, and its quotient is D=O_(Y_s),y. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-fibre-regular-local], L is regular local. The local ring T of affine (a+b)-space over k at h(y) is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth] and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-regular-local]. A minimal generating system of the maximal ideal of L is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], hence L is Cohen--Macaulay.

source.place: Tag 0FUE, local rings on the fibre; divisors.tex Tag 0FUD, algebra.tex Tags 00TT and 00NQ

proof.text: Let Q be the local ring of affine a-space over k at v(y). The last b variables in T form a regular sequence, since multiplication by the next variable is injective on each polynomial quotient and remains injective after localization; their quotient is Q. Repeatedly apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quotient-nonzerodivisor] to get dim L=b+dim D and dim T=b+dim Q. Base change preserves etaleness [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]; its affine comparison [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine] and [lem-sc-etale-local-dimension] give dim D=dim Q. Thus dim L=dim T, also when b=0.

source.place: Tag 0FUE, dimension comparison; more-algebra.tex Tag 07QP; algebra.tex Tag 00KW

proof.text: The closed fibre of T→L is also the closed fibre of Q→D, since all last variables are in the maximal ideal of T and their images are f. It is the local ring of a fibre of the etale map v_s. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] it is a finite separable field extension, so has dimension zero. Now [lem-weil-pbc-miracle-flatness] applies: T is regular, L is Cohen--Macaulay and dim L=dim T+0. Therefore T→L is flat.

source.place: Tag 0FUE, finite local fibre and miracle flatness; algebra.tex Tag 00R4; morphisms.tex Tag 02GL

proof.text: Put R₀=O_(S,s), T₀=O_(A^(a+b)_S,h(y)), L₀=O_(X,i(y)). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-criterion-flatness-fibre] to R₀→T₀→L₀ and the module L₀. Both algebras are essentially finitely presented: they are prime localizations of the affine-space polynomial algebra and the finitely presented ambient algebra. L₀ is a nonzero free rank-one L₀-module, and is flat over R₀ by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. Reduction modulo the maximal ideal of R₀ is the flat map T→L just proved; quotient and localization identify the reductions with the displayed local rings of the fibre. The criterion yields flatness of T₀→L₀.

source.place: Tag 0FUE, fibre criterion; Tag 039C, theorem-criterion-flatness-fibre, algebraic input Tag 00R7

proof.text: On affine charts let P be the polynomial algebra of the target. The localized module N=(Ω_(A/P))_y is finite, since h is finitely presented [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Differential base change [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change], followed by localization, identifies its residue fibre with differentials of the local fibre of h. Localization follows from the universal derivation formula d(u/v)=v⁻¹du−uv⁻²dv. By the cartesian hypothesis that fibre is the corresponding fibre of v, which is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. The affine etale comparison [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine] makes its differential module zero. Hence N modulo the maximal ideal of L₀ is zero. Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators], applied to the empty generating family, gives N=0. Finite presentation, flatness of T₀→L₀, and [lem-sc-etale-at-prime-flat-unramified-criterion] give a principal open T containing i(y) on which this specified h is etale.

theorem Scheme.Hom.exists_etale_open_of_regular_coordinate_fibre
    {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ S) [Smooth p] (i : Y ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (a b : ℕ)
    (h : X ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin (a + b))) S)
    (v : Y ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin a)) S) [Etale v]
    (hh : h ≫ (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin (a + b))) S ↘ S) = p)
    (H : IsPullback v i
      (AffineSpace.homOfVector (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin a)) S ↘ S)
        (fun j ↦ Fin.addCases (fun k ↦ AffineSpace.coord S (ULift.up k))
          (fun _ ↦ 0) j.down)) h)
    (hreg : ∀ W : X.affineOpens,
      RingTheory.Sequence.IsWeaklyRegular Γ(X, W)
        (List.ofFn (fun j : Fin b ↦
          X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : W.1 ≤ ⊤)).op
            (h.appTop (AffineSpace.coord S (ULift.up (Fin.natAdd a j)))))))
    (y : Y) :
    ∃ T : X.Opens, i y ∈ T ∧ Etale (T.ι ≫ h)
